messages.content: Help me generate the XContent with xContentBuilderInstance for a RootObjectMapper that includes default settings for dynamic date formats, dynamic templates, date detection, and numeric detection, while skipping runtime fields?

function.name: RootObjectMapper_doXContent
function.description: Serializes the RootObjectMapper settings to XContent, with options to include default values and to skip runtime fields. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

builder.description: The XContentBuilder to which the content should be written. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

params.description: Parameters controlling the serialization, including whether to include defaults and whether to skip runtime fields. This is Java ArrayList type parameter in string representation. The list elements are of type any; they are not in string representation.

Params: array of strings: ["includeDefaults", "skipRuntimeFields"]. But we need to specify values: includeDefaults=true, skipRuntimeFields=true. So params string representation of Java ArrayList containing two elements: maybe "true" or "false"? The description says parameters controlling serialization, including whether to include defaults and whether to skip runtime fields. So we pass something like ["true","true"].

Thus call:

functions.RootObjectMapper_doXContent({builder:"xContentBuilderInstance", params:["true","true"]})

But the function expects params as string representation of Java ArrayList type parameter in string representation. So we might need to pass JSON string? The example earlier: builder: string, params: string. So we pass builder string "xContentBuilderInstance". For params, we need string representation of Java ArrayList type parameter in string representation. That could be something like "[\"true\",\"true\"]" or maybe "java.util.ArrayList@...". But likely just JSON array string.

Thus output: functions.RootObjectMapper_doXContent({builder:"xContentBuilderInstance", params:"[true,true]"}) but booleans need quotes? In Java arraylist string representation, booleans are true/false without quotes. So string "[true,true]".
